Question: What should you do if you are on foot and suspect someone in a motor vehicle is or has been following you?
Answer: When it happened to me I confronted them. It was Sunday night, winter in Sao Paulo, Brazil. Empty streets and Brazil is not known as a safe country. I was going back home, coming from my ex's house and near a main Avenue and at the lights a car stopped and called me for information. I gave them instructions of how to reach their destination, while I was explaining (it was a couple) the girls used to interrupt and say to her boyfriend “he is so cute” and smile. They thanked me and left. After a few minutes, in a different street, a saw their car, well suspicious, because they weren't following my instructions, but whatever, after like 200 meters, in a intersection I saw their car again, parked and with lights on. This time I thought that they were following me and since I was near home I didn't want them to find out where I lived. I started to walk to towards them and went to the passanger side, where the girl was and I asked them “are you following me?”. She said “how cute, he is scared”. They started to laugh, they would tell me something but she looked at my hand and saw a ring, a relationship ring. She saw that and said “Ah, he has a girlfriend, forget about it”. Then I understood that they were looking for a threesome, probably with a younger man, I was 19, they were between 25–29, she was definitely cute. I would have accepted. My relationship was in rubbles anyway, nothing to lose there. I went home thinking about it. It would be dangerous? Did the couple was looking for another man for her or for him. Would I be able to escape in case of danger? But I was leaning to accept. It never happened again in my life, a couple out of nowhere, inviting me for a threesome.

Question: Are Brazilians one of the worst integrated groups in Ireland?

I had to make a conscious effort to have foreign friends in Dublin and avoid to be around Brazilians all the time and therefore, improve my English. My English would improve usually when I was traveling alone. When we Brazilians are in big groups we are “self sufficient”. We are too “provincial”. We become a closed group, doing Brazilian things and looking for another Brazilians. And we don't like to speak in a different language, which keep our bad language skills in good shape always. Personally I don't see the point to travel to another place and ignore local culture, but that's my point of view. Another Brazilian told me he would like to do Brazilian things in a foreign land.
